primary_users: developers choosing a model/runtime configuration for a workload and device
primary_jobs: choose a use case and find the best evidence-backed model + quantization + configuration for this device
manually test one served model/configuration against a representative scenario
understand what each benchmark contains before trusting its aggregate result
trace aggregate benchmark results down to the individual samples and evaluator evidence that produced them
compare the same benchmark case across model + quantization + configuration candidates
inspect available model candidates, datasets, evaluators and retained evidence without confusing those library objects with the primary decision workflow
understand quality, runtime performance and resource evidence without conflating the dimensions
compare compatible evidence and detect regressions against an explicit compatible baseline

information_architecture.primary_user_question: Which model works best for my workload on this device, and with which configuration?

journey_hierarchy.primary: Find best setup: goal (use case + device) -> candidate models -> optimization -> review -> campaign -> results
journey_hierarchy.direct_manual: Test a model: target/model -> scenario -> test configuration -> review -> live run -> immutable run result
journey_hierarchy.benchmark_first: Library -> Benchmarks -> Benchmark Detail -> benchmark case
journey_hierarchy.run_first: Runs -> Run Detail -> Samples -> Sample Evidence Detail
journey_hierarchy.campaign_first: Find best setup -> Campaign Results -> benchmark case -> Case Comparison Across Candidates
journey_hierarchy.library_inspection: Library -> Models / Benchmarks / Datasets / Evaluators / Evidence -> object detail

evidence_drilldown.aggregate_to_sample: aggregate metric -> contributing benchmark cases -> individual sample outcome -> evaluator evidence
evidence_drilldown.benchmark_definition: benchmark -> test cases -> prompt/input/context -> expected output -> evaluator rules
evidence_drilldown.cross_candidate: same benchmark case -> candidate model + quantization + configuration -> response/outcome/metrics

essential: main quality, performance and resource evidence
advanced: runtime configuration reported by the server
expert_diagnostics: logs only when retained and safe to expose

overview.goal: Answer what decision the user can make next, what has been tested, and what evidence is available.
must_show: decision-first entry into Find best setup before evidence inventory
device/workload context where needed to interpret evidence
separate quality, performance and resource summaries when trustworthy
must_not_show: a cross-cohort winner without explicit compatibility and decision policy

find_best_setup.goal: Choose the best model + quantization + configuration for one selected use case on this device.
rules: campaign and results are lifecycle/outcome states after setup, not setup decisions
benchmark plan and estimate are contextual review information, not mandatory standalone setup steps
use case determines benchmark, dataset and evaluator relevance
device/target is selected with the goal so downstream candidates stay scoped correctly
eligible model candidates are selected by default when the backend has already scoped them to the chosen target
same base model with different quantization is a distinct candidate
quantization is candidate identity, not a sweep parameter
standard search is the preferred normal default when the runtime exposes bounded search ranges; fixed authored configuration is the safe fallback when it does not
request-level parameters may be searched only when declared supported
runtime/model-load parameters may be searched only when the serving runtime exposes an explicit mutable lifecycle
advanced/custom optimization controls are progressively disclosed and never invent parameter ranges or capabilities
review foregrounds candidate/configuration/run scope and next action while benchmark/provenance/fingerprint detail stays contextual or advanced
campaign results require comparable evidence and an explicit versioned decision policy

test_a_model.goal: Run one controlled evaluation of one served model candidate and one frozen configuration.
rules: backend owns endpoint discovery; browser never calls inference runtime directly
model ID should come from discovery when supported
connection details are progressively disclosed
advanced generation/runtime controls do not dominate the common path
runtime-load configuration is observational unless the runtime explicitly supports mutation

campaign.goal: Show bounded progress across model/configuration candidates without replacing run identity.
rules: campaign groups immutable runs
each matrix row maps to one model + quantization + frozen configuration run
running presentation is progress-first: overall progress precedes per-candidate runs
queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled states are explicit
leaving the campaign screen does not imply cancellation when server-owned progress persists
cancellation and failure recovery preserve resource ownership and partial evidence truthfully

campaign_results.goal: Recommend the best fit for the selected use case and explain the trade-off from comparable evidence.
rules: recommend model + quantization + configuration, never model family alone
quality, performance and resources remain separate dimensions
no universal opaque score
reading order is compatibility and decision policy -> recommendation -> evaluator-owned/policy-owned rationale -> candidate comparison -> case-level drill-down
decision policy and compatibility are visible before recommendation
recommendation rationale comes from the backend result contract; the frontend never invents trade-off claims
support alternatives such as highest quality, fastest and lowest resource usage only when evidence supports them
allow drill-down to the benchmark cases that materially differentiate candidates

benchmark_detail.goal: Explain what a benchmark measures before showing how any model performed on it.
rules: benchmark definition and benchmark execution evidence are distinct
do not show a model/run score in the benchmark-definition view unless the user explicitly enters a results context
test case detail may show prompt/input, expected output and evaluator rules when disclosure is permitted
evaluator weights shown here belong to this benchmark/suite context, not globally to the evaluator

run_detail.goal: Inspect one immutable run produced by one model candidate and one frozen configuration.
rules: a Run Detail never mixes multiple model candidates or configurations
cross-candidate comparison is a separate surface/action
aggregate results remain traceable to contributing samples when retained evidence permits it

sample_evidence_detail.goal: Understand exactly what happened for one benchmark case in one run.
must_show_when_available: latency and token evidence with provenance
rules: frontend never invents a reason for a score
if evaluator rationale is absent show Evaluation explanation unavailable
if content was not retained show Content not retained rather than an empty content panel

case_comparison_across_candidates.goal: Compare the same benchmark case across compatible candidate runs.
rules: same benchmark case and compatible benchmark/evaluator protocol are required
candidate identity includes model, quantization and configuration
show response/output only when retained
show sample-level resource data only when attribution is trustworthy
do not infer a winner from non-comparable evidence

models.goal: Inspect model candidates discoverable from connected runtimes and their evidence-relevant identity.
rules: same base model with different quantization appears as a separate candidate
Performance Lab does not imply ownership of model loading
connected/offline primarily describes the endpoint/runtime; model status uses available/resident/unknown semantics when supported
Not comparable is never a model status
capabilities and parameter ranges are reported/discovered, never guessed by the UI

datasets.goal: Inspect dataset definitions and versioned snapshots used by benchmarks and run evidence.
rules: mutable catalog metadata and immutable run-used snapshots are visually and semantically distinct
a run-referenced dataset snapshot remains versioned and immutable
retention UI must not imply silent deletion of evidence required to interpret retained runs
sample preview is allowed only where source/license/privacy policy permits it

evaluators.goal: Inspect evaluator definitions, scoring semantics and evidence requirements.
rules: an evaluator has no universal global weight
weights are shown only in the benchmark/suite or decision-policy context that owns them
LLM-as-judge identity/model/version belongs to evaluator provenance
rationale availability is explicit

evidence_library.goal: Audit retained evidence and provenance across runs/campaigns without bypassing privacy/retention semantics.
rules: aggregate-safe mode does not expose prompt/output content unless explicitly retained by contract
evidence-rich mode may expose retained prompt/output with clear sensitivity and retention context
Content not retained is a first-class state
credentials and authorization material are never evidence
artifact provenance links back to run/campaign, benchmark case, evaluator and source build/environment

compare.goal: Compare evidence only after compatibility has been established.
rules: compatibility reasons appear before deltas
no delta, ranking or regression verdict is shown for incompatible dimensions
quality, performance and resources remain separate

settings.goal: Configure Performance Lab-owned preferences and connections without turning settings into the primary workflow.
rules: do not surface speculative settings for features the product does not own
model connections configure endpoint discovery and credentials safely
runtime/model-load settings remain external unless an explicit mutable runtime contract is adopted
evidence retention settings explain consequences for future sample drill-down
secrets are never shown after storage and never exported into evidence

configuration_search.request_parameters: eligible when supported by the adapter/runtime contract
configuration_search.runtime_load_parameters: eligible only when the serving runtime exposes an explicit mutable configuration lifecycle
configuration_search.quantization: not a sweep parameter; distinct quantizations are distinct model candidates

evidence_inspection.goal: Every aggregate result must be traceable, when retained evidence permits it, to the benchmark cases that produced it and to evaluator-owned evidence explaining each sample outcome.

case_detail: rendered prompt or canonical input when disclosure is permitted

sample_detail: expected output or gold label when available
evaluator-owned rationale or rule evidence when available
latency and token evidence with provenance

cross_candidate_case_comparison.comparison_key: same benchmark case identity under compatible benchmark/evaluator protocol
candidate_fields: resource evidence only when sample-level attribution is trustworthy
cross_candidate_case_comparison.recommendation_reasoning: must derive from explicit comparable evidence and the versioned decision policy; no post-hoc frontend explanation

aggregate-safe.prompt_and_output_content: not retained unless the evaluator contract requires it
aggregate-safe.sample_metrics_and_typed_outcomes: may remain available when stored as aggregate-safe evidence

evidence-rich.prompt_and_output_content: may be retained explicitly for debugging

progressive_disclosure.essential: sample outcome, main evaluator result, key latency/performance facts
progressive_disclosure.contextual: expected vs actual, per-field/per-rule evaluator breakdown
progressive_disclosure.advanced: full prompt/context, complete response, benchmark/evaluator provenance
progressive_disclosure.expert_diagnostics: raw artifacts/logs only when explicitly retained and safe to expose

principles: visualizations answer a concrete comparison, trend, distribution or progress question
quality, performance and resources use distinct semantic encodings
unknown/unavailable/not-comparable are not plotted as zero
confidence or uncertainty is shown when available and material
recommendation emphasis never substitutes for explicit decision-policy evidence
tables are preferred over decorative charts when exact comparison is the primary task
prohibited: charts based on fabricated or unavailable metrics

rules.desktop_compact: preserve primary content; collapse or condense secondary navigation and move optional detail panes below/into an explicit detail surface
rules.desktop_standard: persistent task navigation with one primary content region and optional contextual detail pane
rules.desktop_wide: use additional space for useful side-by-side evidence inspection, never to add decorative density

critical_journeys.name: Choose goal/device -> confirm model candidates -> choose optimization -> review -> run campaign -> understand best-fit result
Connect a model -> test it manually -> understand the result
Find tested-model evidence with workload and device context
Compare two compatible runs -> understand trade-offs
Attempt incompatible comparison -> understand why deltas are invalid
Run fails -> understand cause -> retry successfully
Cancel a run -> resources release -> next run succeeds
Inspect a benchmark -> understand its cases, expected outputs and evaluator rules
Open one immutable run -> inspect contributing samples -> understand one sample outcome from evaluator evidence
Open a campaign result -> inspect one benchmark case across compatible candidates -> understand response and metric trade-offs

visual_target_policy.target_role: design intent reference, not pixel-regression golden
visual_target_policy.implementation_golden_rule: visual-regression goldens are captured from an approved real implementation after semantic, accessibility and journey validation; generated mockups are never used as pixel-diff truth
visual_target_policy.implementation_golden_scope: limited stable high-value target-backed surfaces with exact build/source provenance; not a substitute for semantic, accessibility or representative-user acceptance

validation.accessibility_automation: planned with browser UI: Playwright + accessibility assertions
validation.visual_regression: CI compares the limited stable high-value implementation-golden set after semantic journey coverage; manual accessibility/usability evidence remains a separate reference-grade gate
validation.manual_accessibility: keyboard/focus/contrast review at compact, standard and wide desktop sizes
validation.usability_evidence: representative-user review before reference-grade UI claim
validation.sample_traceability: verify aggregate -> sample -> evaluator-evidence navigation and aggregate-safe/content-not-retained states
validation.cross_candidate_case_comparison: verify same-case identity and comparability before candidate-level response/metric comparison
validation.surface_semantics: verify Run Detail contains one run identity, Benchmark Detail contains definition not execution outcome, evaluator weights are contextual, and model status never substitutes for evidence comparability
